Lane `check/M0-s-02` (Opus, on the owner's Mac — §12.1's reference machine; wave 4, relaunched 2026-10-04 ~03:15),
2026-10-04, implementer-side independent checker, not the item's author (author lane `build/M0-s-02`, LANDED
2026-10-04 04:11, ledger row L-0078, choices C-0153 – C-0158). Protocol: `M0.md` §3 steps 1 – 5. No git was run; no
file of the item was changed; the probes ran on a scratch mirror of `plat/` outside the project (deleted afterwards,
its `node_modules` first), one vitest process at a time, `--maxWorkers=2` (mutants `--maxWorkers=1`).

## Verdict: FAIL — three failing lines (F-1 – F-3); every gate is green

The code is careful and its tests bite: every gate is green, all 22 targeted mutants are red, and the exit bar holds
over every one of the 395 shipped cells. The item fails on three lines:

* **F-1 (CONFIRMED, executed).** The item's own tests pin the values of the cells that M0.md §2's hand-over chains
  give to the run items M0-b-05a, M0-b-05b, M0-c-07a and M0-c-07b. A run item writes no code and cannot edit this
  item's tests (C-0115, C-0117). Simulated on a scratch mirror, each of the four hand-overs turns
  `test --project tables` red, 16 tests in all. This contradicts C-0157 (2)'s stated purpose: "The hand-overs must be
  able to land without editing this item's tests".
* **F-2 (CONFIRMED by reading and a data scan; the parity impact is PLAUSIBLE until M1's presets exist).** The cells
  that §4.6 and §7.6 name as zeroed by the parity presets carry no `extension` marker: the six hidden-share targets,
  and the twelve non-`open` reach weights (`passage`, `gated`). No choices row declares this. C-0154 (4) lists the
  markers it applied (the slope term, `drivers.wealthGradient`, the two soft terms) and omits these.
* **F-3 (CONFIRMED by reading).** `RungProfile.layers` declares `SewerExistenceRow` and `UndercityExistenceRow` under
  the design's names but with other shapes. II.7.4 gives `{ existence; law? }`; the code has a string union. II.7.5
  gives `{ existence; maxNeighbourhoods: 0|1|2|3; minPopulation?; chance? }`; the code has
  `{ rule; max: number; minPopulation?; chance? }`. C-0156 (3) records the shape "as the table states it", naming §1.1
  only, so it does not declare the departure from II.7.4 and II.7.5.

**F-1 — the hand-overs cannot land green.**

M0.md §2 hands these files over:

All four takers are run items, which write no code (M0.md §2; C-0115, C-0117), so they cannot edit
`packages/tables/test/`. C-0157 (2) builds the golden test so that a version bump passes. Its reason column says:
"The hand-overs must be able to land without editing this item's tests". The other tests still pin the handed-over
values:

* `tables.test.ts`:
  * 19: `expect(BAND_IDS.map((b) => t.num(b, 'share'))).toEqual([0.011, 0.011, 0.217, 0.435, 0.217, 0.109])`;
  * 45 – 48: the granularity rows;

  * 97: `expect([flat.value, flat.unit, flat.provenance, flat.calibratable]).toEqual([0.7, 'm', 'own', true])`;
  * 125 – 128: the deep-interior shares;
  * 229: `expect(picks).toBe(81)` over notes whose provenance must stay `own`.
* `bands.test.ts`:

* `loader.test.ts`:
  * 97: `expect(t.num('settings', 'flattenM')).toBe(0.7)`;
  * 145: `version: '1'` for a granularity slice.

The checker simulated each hand-over on the mirror (`scratchpad/waves/check-M0-s-02/handover.mjs`). Each simulation
bumped the file's version and rewrote the handed-over cells with provenance `M-1 2026-10-20`, as the run items will:

```
  tables.test.ts: holds the four default rows …; holds the block-depth floors …
  bands.test.ts: serves the four rowed bands …; interpolates comfortable …; reads the poor row at squalid …;
                 reads a town's cuts …; property: every value reads between the rows …
  loader.test.ts: fills a slice with its version and its hash …
b05b (cut.flattenM)                           exit 1   Tests  2 failed | 172 passed (174)
  tables.test.ts: holds cut.bendMode flatten and cut.flattenM 0.7 m …; loader.test.ts: read numbers, ranges, keys and flags
c07a (deep-interior shares)                   exit 1   Tests  1 failed | 173 passed (174)
  tables.test.ts: holds the deep-interior shares …
c07b (band weights, shares, default cuts)     exit 1   Tests  5 failed | 169 passed (174)
  tables.test.ts: holds the six bands …; carry provenance 'own' and a note naming the lane
  bands.test.ts: has the six bands in order and the default cuts …; places each band at its centre …;
                 switches at the lower cut of the next rowed band above
```

The golden test passed in all four runs; the version bump worked as C-0157 (2) intends. CONFIRMED.

*Required change:*

* `tables.test.ts`: pin a handed-over file's design defaults only while the file is at its `golden.json` version.
  Read the pin; at a higher version assert the invariants instead:
  * ranges ordered;
  * the interior share rows and the band shares sum to one, and the default cuts are the cumulative shares;
  * provenance one of the admitted forms;
  * the census flags unchanged;
  * the picks count taken over cells still at `own` with the lane note.
* `bands.test.ts`: read fixed fixture rows through `parseTable` (a test-owned table, not the live `granularity.json`
  and `bands.json`), or derive its expectations from the loaded rows.
* `loader.test.ts`: derive `flattenM`'s expectation and the slice's version from `loadTable`.
* Re-run the four simulations above until they are green, and record the reading in a choices row.

**F-2 — the `extension` markers of the cells the parity presets zero are missing.**

* §7.6 (12373 – 12375): "set every `extension` cell's chance or weight to 0 and its option off (the hidden-plot
  share, …, the island and sewer rules …)". Its resolution order (12394 – 12395): "its own `presets` entry; else, for
  an `extension` cell, 0 for a chance, a weight or a number and off for an option; else the cell's default".
* §4.6 (7428 – 7429), on the hidden-share targets: "our own values, calibratable; 0 in the parity presets and at every
  village rung". On the reach (7404 – 7406), `open` is "the references' every-plot-fronts-a-street baseline … and the
  parity presets' only value".
* The data: a scan of all 395 cells finds `extension` only on `cut/slope/{thresholdSlope,weightMax,slopeScale}` and
  `fields/prosperity/{wealthGradient,daylight,waterTerm}.weight`. `interior.json`'s six `hiddenShare` cells
  (`{"value": 0.2, "unit": "share", "provenance": "own", "calibratable": true}` …) carry none. Neither do its six
  `reach.passage` and six `reach.gated` cells.
* Under §7.6's order, M1's parity presets would therefore serve the defaults, not 0. No choices row stages or declares
  this, and C-0154 (4) enumerates the markers applied without these cells.
* PLAUSIBLE also: `ladder.json`'s `layers.*` cells, by §7.6's "the island and sewer rules". The reading depends on
  whether the rung row's existence words are the rules §7.6 means; the author should decide this and record it.

*Required change:* add the markers. Suggested readings: `hiddenShare` and `reach.passage` / `reach.gated` as
`{ over: 'both', mode: 'weight' }`, and `layers.*` as decided. Rewrite `golden.json` in the fix round (the files are
still the item's own). Add a test that lists the extension cells. Alternatively, append a choices row naming §4.6 and
§7.6 that stages the markers to M1 with the presets (§4b) and names its test.

## Notes (not failing)

* **N-1.** C-0153 (2)'s name map (⟨table⟩.⟨name⟩ → a row, or a `settings` cell) does not describe several shipped
  addresses:
  * `ways.widths` is stored as each class row's `widthM.<RUNG>` cells;
  * `crossing.searchBandM` is stored at `terrain/crossing/searchBandM`, whereas §7.6 places it in "one base settings
    row", V11's registry, M1;
  * `drivers.wealthGradient` is stored at `fields/prosperity/wealthGradient.weight`;
  * `passage.widthM` is stored at `interior/settings/passageWidthM`.

  The consumers read the files, so the impact is small (PLAUSIBLE). An addendum row listing the exceptions would keep
  the map true.
* **N-2.** C-0154 (2) lists P11 among the P-ids carried, but no P11 cell ships, because §4.2 S3 (4)'s coastal gate
  reduction is not in `walls.json`. C-0154 (3) says "on every seat pick" calibratable is true, while C-0158 excepts
  the strip widths (`walls/era.default` ×3, `false`). The two rows should agree.
* **N-3.** `regimes/heading.planned/{correlationM, reversionM}` (90 m and 250 m) carry `architecture 2026-09-25`.
  §4.4 states only planned's σ (5° per 100 m). Reading the planned setting as sharing organic's ℓ and L_r is
  defensible; a note on the cell would make it explicit.
* **N-4.** The village rows are refused by a `TableError` naming volume 7, not by `notBuilt(...)`. They are declared
  in `defers` and C-0156 (6); accepted.
* **N-5.** The directive at `bands.ts` 104 is accepted on its reason (line 5).
* **N-6.** §4.5's parity step blend ("sets the interpolation's blend to a step at each cut") arrives with the presets
  at M1 (§4b); `bandInterpolate` has no step mode yet.
* **N-7.** `golden.test.ts` passes any content at a higher version. This is by design (C-0157 (2)); the declaration is
  the bump.
* **N-8.** `corepack pnpm test -- --project tables` runs every project, because the root script hands vitest a
  literal `--`. A checker wanting one project uses `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --project tables`.
